init.title: EMS bus logger: connection
init.description: Logs EMS telegrams from an EMS-ESP gateway to daily files. It reads the `watch` output of the EMS-ESP telnet console and sends nothing to the EMS bus.

data_description.ems_host: IP address or host name of the EMS-ESP gateway.
data_description.ems_port: Telnet must be enabled in EMS-ESP (Settings → Services). Default 23.

logger.title: EMS bus logger: what and where
logger.description: EMS-ESP reports {devices} devices; they are offered in the ID fields. Any other hex ID can be typed in.

data_description.ems_filter_ids: Keep only telegrams from or to these devices. Empty: the whole bus. With one ID EMS-ESP filters itself, with several the whole bus is watched and filtered here.
data_description.ems_ignore_ids: Drop telegrams from or to these devices, for example the EMS-ESP gateway itself to leave out its own polling.
data_description.ems_pair_src: Creates sensors for the telegrams from this device to the destination, for example thermostat to boiler. Leave both empty for none.
data_description.ems_log_dir: Absolute path; one file per day. On Home Assistant OS, a folder in /share is outside /config and can be left out of backups.
data_description.ems_compress_after_days: Gzip a day's file once it is this many days old (1 = yesterday's file). 0: never.
data_description.ems_thermostat_id: Creates a presence sensor and a flow request sensor for this bus thermostat, for example for a heating controller that must step back while the thermostat is on the bus. Leave empty for none.
data_description.ems_presence_timeout: Seconds without a telegram from the thermostat until it counts as absent. Thermostats send every few seconds to a minute.

error.invalid_hex: Enter hex IDs such as 08 or 0x08.
error.host_required: Enter the EMS-ESP host to enable the logger.
error.pair_incomplete: Enter both pair devices, or leave both empty.
error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the EMS-ESP console (check host and telnet port; telnet must be enabled in EMS-ESP).
error.dir_not_writable: Cannot create or write to this folder.
error.thermostat_filtered: The filter or ignore list drops this device's telegrams.

state.blocked: Blocked by a zone without valve

user.title: Add heating controller
user.description: Computes the flow temperature a boiler should be asked for, from a heating curve and the demand of the zones. **Shadow mode: it only computes and shows the value and sends nothing to the boiler.**

data_description.outdoor_entity: Any temperature sensor outdoors (or a weather-based sensor).
data_description.thermostat_id: EMS ID of the thermostat that controls the boiler now, to compare its requests and see whether it is on the bus. Needs the EMS bus logger, and the ID must pass its filter. Empty: no comparison.
data_description.presence_timeout: The thermostat counts as present if it sent a telegram within this time.
data_description.design_outdoor: Heating curve: the coldest outdoor temperature it is designed for.
data_description.design_flow: Heating curve: flow temperature at the design outdoor temperature and a 20 °C room.
data_description.min_flow: Lowest flow temperature asked for while heating.
data_description.max_flow: Highest flow temperature ever asked for.
data_description.room_gain: Extra flow temperature per kelvin the neediest zone is below its target.
data_description.summer_limit: No heating at or above this outdoor temperature (frost protection still works).
data_description.boost_offset: Added to the flow temperature while a zone is 1 K or more below its target, for a faster heat-up.
data_description.min_on_minutes: Keep heating at least this long once started.
data_description.min_off_minutes: Wait at least this long before heating again.

user.title: Add heating zone
user.description: A room the controller looks after. Give it a climate entity, or a temperature sensor (then the integration creates a climate entity for the room's target).

data_description.climate_entity: A thermostat of the room (for example a radiator thermostat). Its current temperature and target are used. Leave empty to get a climate entity from this integration for the room.
data_description.temperature_entity: Room temperature. Overrides the climate entity's temperature if both are set. Required without a climate entity.
data_description.valve_entity: Optional, shown for comparison only (for now).
data_description.has_valve: Off for radiators that are always open: the room then stops the heating when it gets too warm.
data_description.weight: Multiplies the room's demand. 1 = normal, 0 = ignore the room.
data_description.comfort_temperature: Target of the comfort preset (only for the integration's own climate entity).
data_description.eco_temperature: Target of the eco preset (only for the integration's own climate entity).
